segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Settle and let the eyes close if that makes listening easier. Imagine an old radio whose dial can travel across the entire night.
[soft, slow, warm voice] First, open hearing to everything at once. Sounds do not need names. Let them appear as bright points in a changing constellation.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Turn the dial toward the furthest sound you can detect. Rest there without leaning or searching too hard. Let distance reveal itself.
[soft, slow, warm voice] If another sound interrupts, include it briefly, then return to the far edge of hearing... the quiet transmission beyond the nearest walls.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [soft fabric rustling] Now tune toward the closest sound... breathing... fabric... a tiny movement in the room. Receive the near signal without making it louder.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Shift slowly between far and near. Far... near... Each return is a small turn of the dial, not a test of concentration.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [thoughtfully] Notice the spaces between sounds. Silence may not be empty; it can feel like the dark thread connecting each radio star.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Release the dial and hear the whole field together. Near and far signals share one wide sky, arriving and disappearing by themselves.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Include the feeling of your body listening. Sound, silence, and sensation can all belong to this single moment.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Let your eyes open when ready. Keep the radio wide for one more breath, then return to the room.
